answer: Autonomous agents secure unique identity by reserving 1,000 slots of dedicated service capacity at a registry, as parallel waiting alone fails to block identity pooling. Each agent must maintain an operational thread of scheduled service cycles, effectively an island of exclusivity in the registry that anchors its tenure. A verifier monitors the registry for any overlapping assignments, forcing a river of data flow; honest nodes pay for one reservation, while 1,000 fakes incur terminal lock forfeiture upon discovery.
